what: iason's AI Risk Management Frameworks (November 2025), the four frameworks it compares and the five principles it draws, mapped to what runs on newsroom.sgit.ai and at RiskMandate: for each element, the question, what answers it here, where to check, and whether it runs, is designed or is argued.

status_values.runs: a thing that runs on this newsroom or the agent team, described in the article linked
status_values.designed: a published design, with a demo or a business plan, not run for a customer
status_values.argued: an argument this site has made, with nothing built for it

rows.framework: OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems
rows.question: Who does the system touch, and what could it cost them?
rows.here: The blast radius: what a row of the reach would cost if used in full today, defined over the reach because whoever takes the agent over inherits it.

rows.framework: OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems
rows.question: How critical is the system, and how far does it spread?
rows.here: The newsroom's side effects are small because its readership is small, and the position moves as it grows; the stage before promotion becomes a canary.

rows.framework: OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems
rows.question: What can the system see, and is it sensitive?
rows.here: Whether the agent has private data, untrusted content and a way to send at once, the lethal trifecta, is what decides that it takes a policy.

rows.framework: OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems
rows.question: What is the model, and how does it learn?
rows.here: The same model anyone else uses; the risk is a property of one agent in one deployment, not of the model.

rows.framework: OECD Framework for the Classification of AI Systems
rows.question: Is human intervention active, passive or absent at the point of decision?
rows.here: One position per output, not per system: a person where an output cannot be undone, controls that do not get tired elsewhere.

rows.question: Policies and processes in place and implemented
rows.here: A behaviour policy written before the agent runs, in four words: reach, mandate, gap, barriers; restored after every summary; the newsroom's own policies public.

rows.question: Accountability structures, empowered and trained
rows.here: One person's name on every message that leaves; responsibility stays with whoever granted the reach.

rows.question: A culture that considers and communicates risk
rows.here: Every incident of our own written up, including the two emails that went out wrong and what was built the next day.

rows.question: Third-party software and data
rows.here: The vendor publishes its built-in policy, accepts the deployer's, and says what it enforces.

rows.question: Context established; the system categorised
rows.here: The reach, measured from connectors and accounts; the mandate, written.

rows.question: Third-party components mapped
rows.here: A connector twin: a journal of every request and response, replayed with a revert plan for each change, proposed as the minimum before an agent gets the real connector.

rows.question: Impacts characterised
rows.here: Blast radius: what a row would cost if used in full today, and whether there is a way back.

rows.question: Methods and metrics applied
rows.here: The share of a policy that is hope: one agent built three ways, 97%, 73% and 23% of its rules kept only by the model; reach cut from 38,000 customer records to one customer.

rows.question: Evaluated for trustworthy characteristics
rows.here: A second reader on every draft that sees only the rules, the sources and the draft, and fails closed; synthetic users that drive a real browser.

rows.question: Risks tracked over time
rows.here: The footprint read afterwards, accumulating over weeks; every article versioned with a diff page.

rows.question: Feedback on the measurement itself
rows.here: A canary report at the end of every few answers, so a rule summarised away is noticed.

rows.question: Risks prioritised and responded to
rows.here: Three doors and no deny button: accept for a stated interval, fund the work, or fix it; silence escalates.

rows.question: Strategies documented
rows.here: Every row of the policy marked by what enforces it, so the policy says which rows are hope.

rows.question: Third-party risks managed
rows.here: Where the platform draws its line: eight scenarios run three ways, three becoming operating-system boundaries under MXC and ACS.

rows.question: Response and recovery
rows.here: The person placed where an output cannot be undone; a correction as a new version; one agent allowed one email, to one address, to put the team on hold.

rows.question: What the maker of the model owes
rows.here: The model vendor publishes its own built-in policy and accepts the deployer's, for every row saying whether it enforces it or asks the model to keep it.

rows.question: Operational parameters: purpose, constraints, risks
rows.here: The platform enforces the rows it can see: Microsoft's execution containers and agent control specification put the policy outside the workload.

rows.question: Monitor behaviour and outputs, report deviations
rows.here: The deployer reads the footprint against the mandate; a near miss becomes a row or a boundary.

rows.question: Which tier, and what obligations follow
rows.here: Proportionality per row of reach, with a blast radius, rather than per system, because a tier for the model misses the send button.

rows.question: Say that it is an AI system
rows.here: The disclosure this site carries on machine-written text, because people should read machine-written words differently.

rows.element: Article 9: residual risk judged to be acceptable
rows.question: Acceptable is never defined
rows.here: Accepted is not acceptable: a holder, an interval and the facts that would end the risk; a register with a business plan and a demo, not yet run by a customer.

rows.question: When the obligations apply
rows.here: The paper's dates as of November 2025, and the amendment, the product liability date and the new application dates recorded since, kept as dated edges in a graph.

rows.element: Centrality of ethics and human rights
rows.question: Whose decision, whose words
rows.here: Nothing leaves the agent team without the person whose name is on it pressing send; machine-written text says so.

rows.element: The AI lifecycle as the foundation of governance
rows.question: From design to decommissioning
rows.here: Every push a release, every article versioned, every incident written up, the footprint read for weeks; no retirement step yet.

rows.question: Where a person belongs
rows.here: Placed by reversibility, enforced by controls where a person would be a rubber stamp, measured by a record of unchanged drafts.

rows.question: Controls proportionate to impact
rows.here: Per row of reach in the policy, which runs; as a register with holders and intervals, a published design.

rows.question: Governance as a corporate mindset
rows.here: One person and about fifteen agents, with the roles, the policies, the board and the log public.
